title: Descent of t-exact coefficient families and canonical comparison maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and its directed set of finite subextensions $E$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. For each $E$ let $R_E=\mathcal O_E$ with uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}},\mathcal D_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ be $R_E$-linear triangulated categories [def-weil-linear-category, def-weil-triangulated-category] with bounded t-structures [def-weil-t-structure]. Suppose their raw scalar localizations $\mathcal C_E=\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}[1/\pi_E]$ and $\mathcal D_E=\mathcal D_E^{\mathrm{int}}[1/\pi_E]$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] have distinguished triangles isomorphic to localized integral triangles, and bounded t-structures whose halves are the isomorphism closures of the images of the corresponding integral halves. Suppose exact t-exact coefficient transition functors $T^{\mathcal C}_{L/E},T^{\mathcal D}_{L/E}$ between rational stages are supplied, with identity and associative tower comparisons. Suppose the corresponding pair categories are triangulated: their objects are $(E,K)$, their morphisms are the directed colimits of morphisms after extension to common finite fields, and their distinguished triangles are those isomorphic to triangles from one finite stage. Suppose the isomorphism closures of finite-stage halves give bounded t-structures there, with truncations and their canonical maps computed at a finite stage.

Let $F_E^{\mathrm{int}}:\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}\to\mathcal D_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ be $R_E$-linear exact functors with specified linear shift comparisons. Assume each preserves the two integral halves. Let $F_E$ be their additive extensions on fractions, and suppose natural isomorphisms $\beta_{L/E}:T^{\mathcal D}_{L/E}F_E\cong F_LT^{\mathcal C}_{L/E}$ are supplied as isomorphisms of exact functors, compatible with their shift comparisons, equal to the identity for $L=E$ and compatible with the tower associators. They define the functor $F_\Omega(E,K)=(E,F_EK)$, acting on a common-stage arrow $u$ by $\beta_{\mathrm{target}}^{-1}F_L(u)\beta_{\mathrm{source}}$.

Then every $F_E$ and $F_\Omega$ is exact and t-exact and restricts to an exact functor of hearts. For each of these functors $F$, every integer $m$, and either sign, there are unique natural isomorphisms
$$\alpha^-_{F,m}:F\tau^{\le m}\cong\tau^{\le m}F,\qquad\alpha^+_{F,m}:F\tau^{\ge m}\cong\tau^{\ge m}F$$
with $\iota_{FK}^m\alpha^-_{F,m,K}=F(\iota_K^m)$ and $\alpha^+_{F,m,K}F(\pi_K^m)=\pi_{FK}^m$, where $\iota^m:\tau^{\le m}\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\pi^m:\mathrm{id}\to\tau^{\ge m}$ are the canonical maps. Composing these and the shift comparison gives $F\mathcal H^j\cong\mathcal H^jF$, where $\mathcal H^j=(\tau^{\ge j}\tau^{\le j})[j]$. The $\alpha$ and cohomology comparisons commute with every $\beta_{L/E}$ and with successive coefficient extensions. At $\Omega$ they are represented by the finite-stage comparisons, independently of further enlargement of the stage.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1)-(2) and Remark 6.8.15 motivate the coefficient categories; agent abstract transport lemma extracted from returned proof Steps 7-10. The proof uses raw localization, isomorphism closures of halves, finite-stage triangles, and uniqueness of truncation comparisons; this abstract assertion is not quoted as a theorem of Bhatt-Scholze.

proof.text: Fix $E$ and write $A=R_E[1/\pi_E]$. On each Hom module the $R_E$-linear map induced by $F_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ extends to the $A$-linear map $f\otimes a\mapsto F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(f)\otimes a$ by [def-weil-module-base-change, def-weil-linear-functor]. In the scalar categories [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], this preserves identity morphisms and composition, since on pure tensors both sides of the composition law are $F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(fg)\otimes ab=F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(f)F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(g)\otimes ab$; bilinearity gives the equality on finite sums. Localize the integral shift comparison $c_K:F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(K[1])\simeq F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(K)[1]$ and its inverse. Naturality on $f\otimes a$ is the integral naturality equation tensored with $a$, using linearity of the shifts and of $c$. The same calculation preserves the iterated shift comparisons. This gives precisely the specified additive $F_E$ with its shift comparison.

source.place: Tags 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product) and 05G4 (algebra-definition-base-change); explicit Hom-module base-change calculation

proof.text: A distinguished triangle of $\mathcal C_E$ is, by hypothesis, isomorphic to $Q_{\mathcal C}(\Delta)$ for an integral distinguished triangle $\Delta$. Step 1 gives $F_EQ_{\mathcal C}(\Delta)=Q_{\mathcal D}F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(\Delta)$, including the third arrow composed with the shift comparison. This is distinguished because $F_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ is exact and the target triangulation is the stipulated localized one. Its isomorphic images are distinguished by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Thus $F_E$ is exact. If $K$ is in either rational half at zero, choose an isomorphism $K\simeq Q_{\mathcal C}(K_0)$ with $K_0$ in the corresponding integral half. Its image is isomorphic to $Q_{\mathcal D}F_E^{\mathrm{int}}K_0$, in the corresponding rational half. Hence $F_E$ preserves both halves at zero. The identity $\mathcal C^{\le m}=\mathcal C^{\le0}[-m]$ and its lower counterpart [def-weil-t-structure], together with the shift comparison, give preservation at every integer $m$.

source.place: Tag 014V (derived-definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories), applied to the assumed localized distinguished triangles; BBD 1.3.16 for t-exactness

proof.text:
For objects $(E_i,K_i)$, choose a common field $L$; these fields form a nonempty directed set by [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Write $X_i=T^{\mathcal C}_{L/E_i}K_i$ and $b_i^L=\beta_{L/E_i,K_i}$. The Hom-group map at $L$ is $h_L(u)=(b_2^L)^{-1}F_L(u)b_1^L$. For $M\supset L$, the tower law reads $b_i^M=\beta_{M/L,X_i}\,T^{\mathcal D}_{M/L}(b_i^L)$ after the supplied associators. Substitution gives
$$h_M(T^{\mathcal C}_{M/L}u)=T^{\mathcal D}_{M/L}((b_2^L)^{-1})\,\beta_{M/L,X_2}^{-1}F_M(T^{\mathcal C}_{M/L}u)\beta_{M/L,X_1}\,T^{\mathcal D}_{M/L}(b_1^L)=T^{\mathcal D}_{M/L}(h_L(u)),$$
where the middle equality is naturality of $\beta_{M/L}$. Thus the $h_L$ are compatible additive Hom maps. The universal property of [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups] gives well-defined additive maps on the Hom colimits; in particular equal representatives have equal images. This proves independence of the common field without assuming that coefficient transition functors are faithful.

source.place: algebra-lemma-directed-colimit (Tag 00D6), the representative description and universal property, applied to the assumed Hom systems; the beta equation is an agent calculation

proof.text: At a common field for three objects, cancellation of the middle comparison gives $h_L(v)h_L(u)=(b_3^L)^{-1}F_L(v)b_2^L(b_2^L)^{-1}F_L(u)b_1^L=h_L(vu)$, and $h_L(1)=1$. Any two composable arrow classes admit such representatives by directedness and the representative clause of [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. These equalities prove the functor laws for $F_\Omega$. Its object assignment and Hom maps are exactly those in the statement. The structural functors $J_E^{\mathcal C}:K\mapsto(E,K)$ and $J_E^{\mathcal D}$ satisfy $F_\Omega J_E^{\mathcal C}=J_E^{\mathcal D}F_E$ on stage objects and arrows, with the identity-field identifications. For later fields the induced identifications are the specified $\beta_{L/E}$.

source.place: algebra-lemma-directed-colimit: representatives at a common upper index; explicit cancellation proves functoriality

proof.text: Give $F_\Omega$ the shift comparison represented at $(E,K)$ by that of $F_E$. This is independent of the stage and natural on every common-stage arrow: for a shift-compatible natural isomorphism $\eta:G\simeq H$ the required square is $c_{H,K}\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]c_{G,K}$, which is assumed for each $\beta$; naturality of $c_{F_L}$ gives the other square. Every distinguished triangle in the pair category is isomorphic to $J_E^{\mathcal C}\Delta$ for a distinguished triangle $\Delta$ of $\mathcal C_E$. Its image is isomorphic, including the shifted third arrow, to $J_E^{\mathcal D}(F_E\Delta)$, distinguished by step 2 and the assumed description of pair triangles. This proves exactness in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Likewise every object in either half is isomorphic to $J_E^{\mathcal C}K$ for a $K$ in that finite-stage half; its image is isomorphic to $J_E^{\mathcal D}F_EK$ in the target half. Shifts give all cutoffs as in step 2 [def-weil-t-structure]. This also shows that each $J_E$ is exact and t-exact: it sends a stage triangle to a declared distinguished triangle, commutes with shifts, and sends stage halves into the stipulated pair halves.

source.place: Tag 014V (derived-definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories); direct use of the pair-triangle and pair-half hypotheses; BBD 1.3.16

proof.text: For $F=F_E$ or $F_\Omega$, preservation of the two halves implies preservation of their intersection, the heart. Apply clause 4 of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]: a short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ in the source heart has a distinguished triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$. Exactness of $F$ gives a distinguished triangle on $FA,FB,FC$, all in the target heart, so the same clause makes its first two arrows a short exact sequence in that heart. The restricted functor is additive because $F$ is additive, and it preserves every short exact sequence. This is the claimed exact functor of hearts.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.6 and Proposition 1.3.17(i); apply the short-exact-sequence/distinguished-triangle criterion

proof.text: The bounded t-structures for both rational stages and pair categories are hypotheses. Steps 2 and 5 verify exactness with specified shifts and preservation of both halves at every cutoff. Thus [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] applies to each $F_E$ and to $F_\Omega$. It gives both natural isomorphisms $\alpha^-_{F,m}$ and $\alpha^+_{F,m}$, their uniqueness, and exactly the equations $\iota^m_{FK}\alpha^-_{F,m,K}=F(\iota^m_K)$ and $\alpha^+_{F,m,K}F(\pi^m_K)=\pi^m_{FK}$. In particular these are comparisons with the canonical maps, rather than unspecified objectwise truncation isomorphisms.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i),(ii), pp. 29-30, as packaged in the existing canonical t-exact comparison lemma

proof.text:
Fix $E\subset L$ and either truncation $\tau$ at $m$. Both composites $G=T^{\mathcal D}_{L/E}F_E$ and $H=F_LT^{\mathcal C}_{L/E}$ are exact and preserve both halves: apply preservation for the two factors in succession. Apply the natural-transformation and composition clauses of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to $\eta=\beta_{L/E}:G\simeq H$. Writing the same symbol $\tau$ for the respective stage truncations, its equality is explicitly
$$\alpha_{F_L,T^{\mathcal C}_{L/E}K}\,F_L(\alpha_{T^{\mathcal C}_{L/E},K})\,\beta_{L/E,\tau K}=\tau(\beta_{L/E,K})\,\alpha_{T^{\mathcal D}_{L/E},F_EK}\,T^{\mathcal D}_{L/E}(\alpha_{F_E,K}).$$
This proves beta compatibility for each sign. For $E\subset L\subset M$, the composition clause identifies the comparison for each composite transition with the successive comparisons; apply the transformation clause also to the supplied tower associators. Substituting the assumed beta tower identity into the displayed equality makes the result for $M/E$ identical to its result first for $L/E$ and then for $M/L$. The identity clause deals with $L=E$.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i),(ii): natural-transformation, identity and composition clauses of the cited comparison lemma, applied to the supplied beta and tower isomorphisms

proof.text:
Put $N=\tau^{\ge j}\tau^{\le j}K$ and let $c^j_{F,N}:F(N[j])\simeq(FN)[j]$ be the iterated shift comparison. Define
$$q_{F,j,K}=\bigl(\tau^{\ge j}(\alpha^-_{F,j,K})\,\alpha^+_{F,j,\tau^{\le j}K}\bigr)[j]\,c^j_{F,N}:F\mathcal H^jK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^jFK.$$
All three factors are natural isomorphisms, so this is a natural isomorphism. For a shift-compatible transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$, use the transformation equation of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] first for the lower truncation at $\tau^{\le j}K$ and then for the upper truncation at $K$. After shifting their composite and using $c^j_G\eta_{N[j]}=\eta_N[j]c^j_F$, the resulting equation is
$$q_{G,j,K}\,\eta_{\mathcal H^jK}=\mathcal H^j(\eta_K)\,q_{F,j,K}.$$
The composition clause for both alpha factors and the composite shift comparison give $q_{HF,j,K}=q_{H,j,FK}\,H(q_{F,j,K})$. Applying these equations to step 8 proves all beta, identity and successive-extension compatibilities for cohomology. Negative $j$ uses the inverse shift comparisons; the calculation is unchanged.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3 and the convention H^j(K)=H^0(K[j]) in 1.3.6; explicit composition of the two canonical comparisons with the specified shift comparison

proof.text:
For either truncation let $\gamma_{E,K}^{\mathcal C}:J_E^{\mathcal C}\tau_EK\simeq\tau_\Omega J_E^{\mathcal C}K$ be its finite-stage computation isomorphism from the hypotheses, and similarly for $\mathcal D$. These isomorphisms respect the canonical maps by hypothesis, so uniqueness in [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison], applied to the exact t-exact $J_E$ of step 5, identifies them with the canonical comparisons for $J_E$. Apply that lemma's composition clause to $F_\Omega J_E^{\mathcal C}=J_E^{\mathcal D}F_E$ from step 4. It gives
$$\alpha_{F_\Omega,J_E^{\mathcal C}K}\,F_\Omega(\gamma^{\mathcal C}_{E,K})=\gamma^{\mathcal D}_{E,F_EK}\,J_E^{\mathcal D}(\alpha_{F_E,K}).$$
Thus, under the prescribed identifications, the comparison at $(E,K)$ is represented by the comparison at $E$. Replacing $E$ by $L\supset E$ gives the same morphism: the compatibility equation of step 8 is precisely the equation after the common-stage identifications by beta and the transition-truncation comparisons. Hence it is independent of further enlargement. Naturality for arbitrary pair arrows follows either from step 7 or by putting the arrow and these comparisons at its common field and using their stage naturality. Applying the formula of step 9, with shifts also computed at a stage, proves the identical finite-stage representation and independence assertions for $q$.
